{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom body line (stroke 2), which carries the fall from the start round the lower half of the fish to the nose. I then built the lower tail lobe (stroke 6) and joined it to the body. Together these make up a large share of the fish's outline, and the judge recognizes a fish mainly from that outline. By the end, the start carried through nearly everything standing.

Execution: I took the bottom line early, laid it in steady batches by tracing from the pad, and had it done by about 2:30. I moved straight on to the tail lobe, picking up the join near the lower body. I inspected my areas closely several times, and stood one domino back up at the tail joint so the chain stayed intact. After that I kept my hands off the finished body so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I claimed my strokes clearly and out loud, and I told Tom and Leo to take other work so we weren't crowding each other. That kept bumps down in a small space. When the fin wasn't catching, I looked at it from a distance and told Tom where the break was and how to fix it with a connect. I then stayed clear so he could work. I also confirmed handoffs and stayed in sync with Leo on the tail lobes.

Leadership: I took ownership of a full section without being assigned it. I kept the plan simple and the work divided, and I gave clear status updates during the build. In the last minutes I helped set the discipline of hands off the body until the push. I stayed calm and reliable throughout, and the fish was fully connected when the clock ran out.", "my_share_percent": 30}
